facts.text: Salamanca sits northeast of Madrid’s historic center, offering a quieter, upscale feel while still close to the capital.
In 1625 King Philip IV erected a defensive wall that kept Salamanca confined until the walls were torn down in 1860.
The 1857 Plan Castro, approved by Minister Claudio Moyano, marked the first official expansion of Salamanca beyond its medieval limits.
Don José de Salamanca y Mayol, the 1st Marquess of Salamanca, lent his name to the district after championing its urban development.
Today, Salamanca ranks among Madrid’s most expensive neighborhoods, with real‑estate prices reflecting its affluent reputation.
The IE Business School, once Instituto de Empresa, sits in Salamanca and consistently ranks in the world’s top ten business schools.
